solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Green university put into confusion when name's advanced

parts.note: U is the standard abbreviation for university

indicators.note: moving the name abbreviation further forward rearranges the order of the letters in the confusion word

parts.note: to throw into confusion is to derange

explanation.surface: A university is thrown into chaos when someone's name is pushed up a list.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the standard abbreviation for name; moving a single letter forward is a rare Mephisto device.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone green is young and inexperienced, just as a person below the legal age is.

clue.text: Labour eagerly reveals number one constituent?

indicators.note: the phrase reveals what lies inside it, so the letters are found spanning those two words

parts.note: found across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Labour supporters eagerly show who their top member is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number one' is nursery slang for urine, not a leader; the question mark flags the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Urea is a principal nitrogenous compound found in urine, which children call doing a number one.

clue.text: Angrily carp on about people concerning red herring

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go about, that is around, the next piece
acting angrily is acting wildly, so the following letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, to be mixed up
on means concerning, as in a book on birds; it joins the mix
folk are people

explanation.surface: Someone complains furiously about people who distract with a red herring.
explanation.walkthrough: A Norfolk capon is a humorous old name for a kipper, so 'red herring' is meant literally: a smoked fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Norfolk capon is jocular slang for a red herring, the smoked fish once cheap food in East Anglia.

clue.text: Loose rear, I had … this?

indicators.note: loose letters are not held in place, so they can be rearranged freely

parts.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to a loose rear and asks what the trouble was.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: having a loose rear describes the condition itself. The American spelling is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Diarrhoea is the condition of frequent watery bowel movements, which is exactly what a loose rear describes.

clue.text: Queen about to trap on the first file?

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece placed on another sits below it, so this piece follows

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a gin is a snare, and to gin is to trap
chess board files are lettered from a to h, so the first file is a

explanation.surface: A queen is about to capture something on the opening file of a chessboard.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture of a queen trapping a piece hides the plain charade; only the lettered files of the board matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Regina is the Latin word for queen, used in the formal title of a reigning British monarch.

clue.text: Terrible ordeal, bitten by an insect by stealth

indicators.note: a thing bitten by jaws sits inside them, so this goes within the outer pieces
something terrible is badly wrong, so these letters come out in a different order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a bee is an insect
an is the article a

explanation.surface: A dreadful ordeal: being stung by an insect that crept up unseen.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged ordeal sits between A and BEE.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase à la dérobée, borrowed into English, means secretly or furtively, done without being seen.

clue.text: Homebuyer so upset with ramshackle house wanting new beginning?

indicators.note: upset things are knocked over and disordered, so these letters get mixed
a ramshackle thing is falling apart, so its letters may appear in any order
wanting means lacking, so these letters are taken away from the mix

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be mixed
taken as written, in any order, the letters to remove

explanation.surface: A disappointed homebuyer turns down a tumbledown house and wants a fresh start.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the letters of HOUSE from HOMEBUYER SO and the rest rearranges to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An embryo is the earliest stage of an organism, a new life just beginning; the question mark marks the playful phrasing.

clue.text: Old man's shed in city garden

indicators.note: to shed is to cast off, so this part is dropped from the larger word

parts.note: the capital of Iraq
one's old man is one's father

explanation.surface: A garden shed belonging to an old man, somewhere in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' looks like a garden building but is a verb: DAD is shed from the end of BAGHDAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagh is the Hindi and Urdu word for a garden or orchard, found in Chambers as an Anglo-Indian term.

clue.text: Nip back to pass by Italian market town

indicators.note: going back means reading the word from its end to its start

parts.note: to nip is slang for to steal, or rob
to pass a turn in a game is to go

explanation.surface: Someone pops back to drive past an Italian market town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nip back' reads as a quick return trip; nip here means steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Borgo is the Italian word for a small market town or village, used in English for such places.

clue.text: Fashion retailer and good primarily

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape or form, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the word is used

parts.note: the opening letter of good

explanation.surface: A clothing retailer that is, above all, a good one.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a top fashion retailer is what the answer names.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand atelier is a leading haute couture house, a major studio that designs and sells high fashion.

clue.text: Ornament I fasten round back of neck during greeting

indicators.note: something happening during an event falls inside it, so these letters go within the greeting

parts.note: hi is an informal greeting

indicators.note: turning something round makes it face the other way, so these words are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
to tie is to fasten

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the final letter of neck

explanation.surface: Someone ties a pendant round a friend's neck while saying hello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' looks like part of the necklace picture, but it turns the fastening words backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A hei-tiki is a Maori carved greenstone pendant worn around the neck as a treasured charm.

clue.text: Gathering around Dorothy, actress once dear

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the gathering word is wrapped about the actress

parts.note: a bee is a social gathering for work, as in a sewing bee
Dorothy Lamour was an American film actress of the Road to movies

explanation.surface: A crowd gathers around Dorothy, a former film star who was much loved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks an archaic word: the answer is Spenserian.
explanation.definitionFit: Bel-amoure is an old Spenserian term for a sweetheart or beloved, someone held dear in former usage.

clue.text: Top four for Arsenal, fantastic for periods of time

indicators.note: fantastic means fanciful or bizarre, so the kept letters are rearranged
the top four of a word are its first four letters, so only those are kept

parts.note: the first four letters of the football club's name

explanation.surface: Finishing in the top four is a fantastic achievement for Arsenal, for once.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal is a London football club, and 'top four' sounds like a league table.
explanation.definitionFit: Eras are long spans of history marked by a particular character, so the word means periods of time.

clue.text: Breed of hen flourishing in a rural spot

indicators.note: a flourish is an extravagant flourishing movement, so the letters are waved into a new order

parts.note: the ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A breed of hen thriving out in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australorp is an Australian breed of black domestic chicken developed from the Orpington.

clue.text: Grilling party intelligence largely accepts answer

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the shortened word holds the next letter
largely means mostly but not entirely, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: brain is used to mean intelligence
A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: An interrogation of a spy ring that mostly takes in an answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grilling' suggests questioning but means cooking over coals; BRAI(n) takes in A.
explanation.definitionFit: A braai is a South African barbecue, a social event where meat is cooked over an open fire.

clue.text: Panic-stricken following a reflex attack

indicators.note: reflex means bent back, so the preceding pair is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
taken as written
a raid is a sudden attack

explanation.surface: Someone is terrified after an instinctive attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflex attack' reads as a knee-jerk assault; reflex really turns F A round.
explanation.definitionFit: Being afraid is being frightened, so it matches someone gripped by sudden terror and alarm.

clue.text: Pressing swelling squeezing out head

indicators.note: squeezing out the head of a word removes its first letter

parts.note: turgent is an old word for swelling or turgid

explanation.surface: A boil that needs pressing so the head can be squeezed out.
explanation.walkthrough: TURGENT is a rare Chambers word; drop its T.
explanation.definitionFit: A pressing matter needs immediate attention, which is exactly what urgent describes.

clue.text: Drills around Angola for fuels

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the drills word encloses the country's letters

parts.note: to bore is to drill
AN taken as a short code for the African country

explanation.surface: Drilling for fuel in Angola, an oil-producing country.
explanation.walkthrough: Angola really is an oil producer, which makes 'drills' and 'fuels' feel like one story about oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Boranes are compounds of boron and hydrogen, studied as high-energy rocket and jet fuels.

clue.text: Vexed expression of dismay after piece of wood's thrown over burial ground

indicators.note: after means coming behind, so these pieces are placed later than the wood piece
a thing thrown over is flipped end to end, so this word reads upwards

parts.note: a log is a piece of wood
something that got you vexed or annoyed you
ha can express grief or dismay as well as surprise

explanation.surface: Someone cries out in annoyance when a log is tossed over a cemetery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vexed' is a past participle used for the slangy sense of being got at or annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Golgotha was the hill of the crucifixion, named the place of the skull, and came to mean a graveyard or charnel house.

clue.text: I provided groundwork that shows level of upheaval

parts.note: taken as written
so can mean provided that, as in so long as
a base is a foundation or groundwork

explanation.surface: Someone claims to have laid the foundations that reveal how much upheaval there was.
explanation.definitionFit: In geology an isobase is a contour line joining points of equal uplift of the land since glaciation.

clue.text: Shook with fear at not having succeeded, possibly? Not me!

definitions.text: Shook with fear at not having succeeded, possibly? Not me!

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several arrangements, so the letters may be rearranged
not having means lacking, so this letter is taken out of the fodder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone denies they trembled with fright at failing.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of SHOOK goes, and the rest of SHOOK FEAR AT rearranges; the whole clue is what a brave person would say.
explanation.definitionFit: A heart of oak is a brave, resolute person, someone who would never tremble in terror.

clue.text: Cornerstone awry once bent by heel of trowel

parts.note: skew means askew or awry
corbe is an obsolete word for crooked or bent

indicators.note: the heel is the bottom or back end, so only the word's last letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of trowel

explanation.surface: A builder's cornerstone has gone crooked after being knocked by the end of a trowel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks CORBE as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: A skew corbel is the stone at the foot of a gable that supports the coping, a kind of corner stone.

clue.text: Hospital to get on well with a cut nicking hip

indicators.note: nicking means stealing away, taking a thing inside, so this word holds the next one
something given a cut is trimmed, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: two people who click get on well
hip means fashionable, or in

explanation.surface: At hospital, a patient gets on well despite a cut on the hip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' and 'hip' paint an injury; CLIC(k) holds IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A clinic is a medical centre where outpatients are seen, part of or akin to a hospital.

clue.text: Times about to swagger, it covers come rain or shine

definitions.text: it covers come rain or shine

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the times word wraps around the swagger word

parts.note: by means times in multiplication, as in three by four
to roll is to walk with a swagger

explanation.surface: A newspaper is about to strut, and it shelters readers whatever the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' is not the newspaper but the multiplication sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A brolly is an umbrella, which can shelter you from showers and also serve as a sunshade.

clue.text: Up north everyone retired may do bargain stores

indicators.note: retired means gone back, so the concealed letters read in the opposite direction
a phrase that stores something keeps it inside, so the letters lie within these words

parts.note: found across the three words, then read backwards

explanation.surface: Pensioners in the north may all go to discount shops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up north' marks a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots, a body means a person, so the phrase stands for anyone or any person at all.

clue.text: Borders of gauze section added to sheer dress fabrics

indicators.note: added to means joined onto, so these pieces follow the sheer word

parts.note: sheer can mean bare or unadorned, as in sheer rock

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its outside edges, so only its first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of gauze
S is an abbreviation for section

explanation.surface: Gauze edging is sewn onto sheer dress materials.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface words gauze, sheer and dress all sound like fabric talk, but only 'dress fabrics' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Barège is a light gauzy fabric of wool and silk or cotton, used for women's dresses and veils.

clue.text: Fancy pigeon that is cooking on the grill?

parts.note: the barb is a breed of fancy pigeon
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A prize pigeon ends up being grilled on the coals.
explanation.walkthrough: Barbie is Australian slang for a barbecue.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbie is an informal barbecue, an outdoor meal of food cooked over a grill.

clue.text: Folk dance headed by shy bride's neat

indicators.note: being headed by something means it takes over the front, so the dance's first letter is swapped for this word

parts.note: the kolo is a Serbian and Croatian ring dance
to shy is to throw, as is to lob

explanation.surface: A folk dance is led by a timid bride with a tidy look.
explanation.walkthrough: Neat is an old word for cattle; LOB replaces the K of KOLO.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobolo is the southern African bride price, traditionally paid to the bride's family in cattle.

clue.text: Worthless darts returned having lost points

indicators.note: having lost something means it is gone, so those letters are removed
returned means sent back, so the word reads in the other direction

parts.note: darts are called arrows in pub slang
S and W are compass points

explanation.surface: A worthless darts throw that came back without scoring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Points' sounds like darts scoring but means compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: Orra is a Scots word meaning odd or spare, and hence of little use or value.

clue.text: Number barperson's regularly put on?

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: A garment a bar worker routinely wears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' means an item of clothing, as in a little black number.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron is a protective garment tied over clothes, which bar staff regularly wear on shift.

clue.text: Jailhouse Rock's No 1, it's making a comeback

indicators.note: coming back means returning the way it came, so the letters run backwards
the number one letter of a word is its first, so only that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of Rock
taken as written

explanation.surface: Elvis's Jailhouse Rock, once a number one hit, is returning to the charts.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir is slang for prison, so a jailhouse is the place someone does time in stir.

clue.text: Promoted I advanced avoiding acting like a mercenary?

indicators.note: avoiding means keeping clear of, so this letter is left out of the word

parts.note: a product promoted to buyers is sold
taken as written
an advanced date is an early one
A is the abbreviation for acting, as in a rank

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of being promoted and advancing by not doing what a hired gun does.
explanation.walkthrough: The A goes from EARLY. The question mark admits a mercenary is a hired fighter rather than a soldier proper.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldierly means behaving in the manner of a fighting man, and a mercenary is a paid fighter.

clue.text: Resent deputy deficient in nothing

indicators.note: being deficient in something means lacking it, so that letter goes

parts.note: an envoy is a representative or deputy
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone resents a deputy who has nothing to offer.
explanation.definitionFit: To envy someone is to begrudge them their good fortune, a feeling of resentful longing.

clue.text: Large rodent? Better to prevent one crossing yard

indicators.note: crossing means passing over and taking in, so the pieces go either side of the yard letter

parts.note: to cap something is to better it
to bar is to prevent
a means one
Y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: Keeping one large rat from getting across the yard is the better plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crossing' puts the yard letter where the rodent would cross, between the better and prevent-one pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The capybara of South America is the biggest living rodent, so it is literally a large one.
